title: feat(app-shell): the screen-flow dialog renders a screen field's declared bound, help text and lookup target (objectui#9248)
body:
Fixes #9248
Clause-②: no

The three screen-field keys that objectstack-ai/objectstack#17306 (ruling A, 「声明即强制」) added now render in the console's screen-flow dialog. They are read straight off the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0 `ScreenFieldSpec`, with the spec's own spellings: `min` / `max`, `inlineHelpText`, `reference`. There is no local spelling and no alias. That card holds itself open until these keys render, so this PR supplies the rendering half.

Implemented by the `domain:ui` seat-2 dispatch of session `https://claude.ai/code/session_011p7ikEivgXefNDaE5S5Uec`, branch `claude/issue-9248-screen-field-bound-help-reference`.

## What changed

- **`ScreenView` / `ScreenFieldInput`**
  - A numeric input (`number` or `currency`) gets `min` / `max` as native attributes. They are never written onto a date or text input.
  - `inlineHelpText` is drawn as its own element under the control. Every control arm names it in `aria-describedby`: text, number, textarea, checkbox, select and lookup. The placeholder is left alone, because the browser clears it on the first keystroke.
  - A `type: 'lookup'` field with a non-empty `reference` renders the object form's own `LookupField`, fed the screen's `dataSource`. It is reached through `getLazyFieldWidget('lookup')` from `@object-ui/fields`, the same seam `ActionParamDialog` uses, so no new picker is written. It has its own Suspense boundary, because the Studio preview renders this body with none around it.
  - A lookup with **no** `reference` keeps today's plain input. The spec's `ScreenFieldSpec.reference` doc names that fallback for a run suspended before the key existed.
  - New pure helper `screenFieldBoundViolations(screen, values)`.
- **`FlowRunner`**: the submit check refuses an out-of-bound value beside the `required` check and names the field. The message uses the existing pack keys `validation.min` / `validation.max` / `validation.formInvalidJoiner`, so no i18n key is added. The header's "deliberately not localized" list gains `inlineHelpText` (premise 6).
- **One widening outside the dispatch's two named files, declared here:** `metadata-admin/previews/screen-spec.ts` (`toScreenFields`). It now carries the same four keys into the Studio preview's `ScreenSpec`, each only when it holds the spec's declared type. Premise 5 below explains why.
- One changeset, `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`.

## Premises re-measured

Measured at objectui BASE `3ab51503b`, against the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0 and objectstack tag commit `0f6dcac5e9`.

1. **Spec.** `ScreenFieldConfigSchema` parses `{type:'number',min:1,max:10}`, `{inlineHelpText}` and `{type:'lookup',reference:'account'}`. It refuses a lookup with no `reference` (a custom issue on path `reference`). `help` and `helpText` are **refusals** carrying a rename prescription (`unrecognized_keys`, "Did you mean `helpText` → `inlineHelpText`"), not accepted aliases. objectui reads none of them.
2. **Type.** The 17.5.0 `ScreenFieldSpec` in `@objectstack/spec/contracts` declares `min`, `max`, `inlineHelpText` and `reference`, all optional. They are read off the verbatim re-export, with no local widening.
3. **Rendering reach.** All three `FlowRunner` hosts pass `dataSource`: `useConsoleActionRuntime`, `RecordDetailView`, and the console's `FlowRunsPage`, which passes its adapter. The Studio preview passes its adapter too. So the lookup reaches a data source through `ScreenView`'s existing prop, and the FlowRunner lookup pin runs through that path.
4. **Engine rule.** Measured on `validateScreenInputs` in `service-automation`'s `screen-input-contract.ts` at `0f6dcac5e9`. The bound is compared only when the value is a present finite number, whatever the field's `type`. A value below `min` or above `max` is refused, so the bounds themselves pass (inclusive). A field hidden by `visibleWhen` is skipped. `screenFieldBoundViolations` applies exactly this comparison, and a pin covers each clause.
5. **Falsified.** The Studio preview does reuse `ScreenView`, but `buildScreenSpec` projects each authored field down to `name` / `label` / `type` / `required` / `visibleWhen` in `toScreenFields`. The new keys therefore never reached the preview's renderer. The evidence is the `preview-projection` ablation leg below: with the BASE projection restored, the three preview pins go red. Following the ruling's intent that the keys ship with their rendering, the projection now carries the four keys. This is the only file outside the dispatch's surface.
6. **Translation overlay.** `inlineHelpText` is **not** overlaid. `FLOW_SCREEN_FIELD_COPY_KEYS` is `['label', 'placeholder']` at 17.5.0 and on objectstack main. The spec's translation face also refuses an `inlineHelpText` entry loudly (`unrecognized_keys` on `flows.F.screens.S.fields.Q`), and the spec documents this as a not-yet that needs a ruled widening of that face. The runner walks the constant, so it will follow with no edit here.

## Tests

All of these ran on HEAD `7d9c24c28`, from the worktree root.

- New pins: `ScreenView.boundHelpReference-9248.test.tsx`, `__tests__/FlowRunner.bounds-9248.test.tsx` and `metadata-admin/previews/ScreenPreview.boundHelpReference-9248.test.tsx`. Together they hold 24 tests, one lit leg per key, each with its control:
  - `min: 1, max: 10` puts both native bounds on the input. Submitting 11 or 0 is refused naming the field, and no resume request is sent. Submitting 10 passes and resumes with `{qty: 10}`. An empty optional field is not refused and resumes with `{}`. CONTROL: the same field without the keys resumes with 11.
  - `inlineHelpText: 'Shown below'` renders **below** the input (document order), is linked by `aria-describedby`, becomes the accessible description, and stays on screen while the input holds a value. This holds on every control arm.
  - `type: 'lookup', reference: 'account'`: the picker lists `account` records from the data source. The pin asserts the queried object name, and it renders with no `SchemaRendererProvider`, so only `ScreenView`'s `dataSource` prop can feed it. The same test runs through `FlowRunner`'s host `dataSource` and in the Studio preview. CONTROL: a lookup without `reference` stays a text box.
  - CONTROL: a field carrying none of the keys has no bounds, no `aria-describedby`, no help element and no picker.
- Consumer suites: every test file that names `ScreenView` / `FlowRunner` / `screen-spec` / `buildScreenSpec` / `ScreenPreview`, enumerated with `git grep -l`.
  - Group A: `Test Files 31 passed (31)`, `Tests 378 passed (378)`.
  - Group B (the `RecordDetailView` suites): `Test Files 37 passed (37)`, `Tests 228 passed (228)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`, run after the closure build `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'` (28 of 28 tasks), exits 0. Both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` ran, and `--listFilesOnly` shows all three new pins in the test program.
- Root `scripts/__tests__/` (run once because the diff adds a markdown changeset): `Test Files 177 passed | 2 skipped (179)`, `Tests 5370 passed | 2 skipped`.

## Ablations

These were one-shot runs; no permanent file came from them. Each leg went through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode: the anchor had to hit exactly once, the mutation was proven on disk by a blob change, the three pin files were run, and the restore was proven (blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty). An outer `trap` restored the tree on EXIT, INT and TERM. No dist is involved: the pins import the subject by relative path from `src`.

| leg | mutation | pins red | controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| bound-attr | delete the `min=` / `max=` props on the Input | 4 of 24 (ScreenView x2, FlowRunner x1, preview x1) | green |
| submit-refusal | `if (outOfBounds.length)` becomes always-false | 2 of 24 (11 refused, 0 refused) | green |
| help-text | `helpId` becomes always `undefined` | 4 of 24 | green |
| lookup | the lookup branch is unreachable | 3 of 24 (ScreenView, FlowRunner, preview) | green, including "no reference stays a text box" |
| preview-projection | remove the four carried keys in `toScreenFields` (the BASE projection) | 3 of 24 (all preview pins) | green |

Every leg ended with `ok restored` and a clean tree.

**The control, measured byte-for-byte.** A throwaway probe rendered key-less fields covering every arm, with empty and with filled values, plus the whole `FlowRunner` dialog. It ran against HEAD and against BASE's `ScreenView.tsx` / `FlowRunner.tsx`, with the blob verified equal to `3ab51503b` before the run. Result: `cmp` byte-identical, 21501 bytes each. The files were restored to their HEAD blobs, and `git diff HEAD` came back empty.

## Gates

- eslint on the 6 lintable changed files exits 0 (0 errors). This is a declared narrowing, and all three pieces of evidence are here:
  - The population comes from eslint's own config. The 7th changed file, the `.changeset` markdown, answers "File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied."
  - The count, 6, comes from the `--format json` result length.
  - Invariance: `--print-config` shows no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware. No rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem. So this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exits 0 ("6 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)").
- `check:control-bytes` exits 0.
- `check:new-line-citations` exits 0 (`0 new citation(s)`).
- `check:i18n-keys` exits 0.
- `check:changeset-claims` exits 0 and is report-only. It names two pending changesets that mention `screen-spec.ts`. Both paragraphs are about that file's spec imports, which this change leaves alone, so both still hold.
- `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit` and `check-changeset-no-major` exit 0.
- `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the changed paths answers `NOT GOVERNED`.
- `check:designer-field-key-parity` exits 0.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:eager-closure`, because it needs a full console build, and CI owns it. `ScreenView`'s one new static import is `@object-ui/fields`, which both runtime hosts already import statically through `ActionParamDialog`. `LookupField` itself stays behind the registry's lazy chunk.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, reported to the seat and not changed here:** the Studio preview's `toScreenFields` also drops `options`, `placeholder` and `defaultValue`, all keys that `ScreenView` renders.
  - A one-shot probe on the real `ScreenPreview` gave, for a `select` field with `options` and a text field with `placeholder`: preview `combobox 0 | textbox 1 | placeholder 0` against runtime `combobox 1 | textbox 0 | placeholder 1`.
  - Named producer: objectstack `examples/app-todo` flow `task.flow.ts`, screen node `screen_1`, fields `priority` (`select` with `options` and `defaultValue: 'normal'`) and `category`.
  - It is left alone here because `defaultValue` carries the engine's `{token}` interpolation, which makes the class fix non-mechanical. It also predates this change: the byte-identical control above covers the key-less path.
- `inlineHelpText` is drawn untranslated until the spec's per-field translation face lists it (premise 6). The spec owns that step. Noted, not filed.
- `ScreenView.tsx` eslint warnings go from 12 to 13: one more `react-refresh/only-export-components`, for the new exported helper. The file's existing exported helpers already trip the same rule, and `lint.yml` sets no `--max-warnings`.
- Docs: no objectui guide page documents the flow screen-field contract. That contract is the spec's.
- Not measured: whether the Studio flow designer's screen-field editor offers columns for the new keys. That is an authoring surface outside this card.
